sahneler.metin: This is the disaster that ended the age of the airship.
May sixth, 1937. The German zeppelin Hindenburg arrives over New Jersey.
It is longer than three jumbo jets, lifted by seven million cubic feet of hydrogen.
As it moors to the tower, a spark finds the leaking gas.
In just thirty four seconds, the entire ship is swallowed by fire.
Thirty six people die, and a radio reporter breaks down live on air.
Hydrogen was cheap to make. It was also violently flammable.
No passenger airship was ever trusted again.
One spark ended an entire era of flight.
